newsitem.title: UK: LME copper prices steady after slip on kerb.
newsitem.headline: LME copper prices steady after slip on kerb.

text.p: Copper prices steadied on the London Metal Exchange (LME) during Monday evening after losing their way late in the afternoon kerb session.
The red metal was indicated at $1,930/$1,934 on 1800 GMT having recovered a couple of dollars from its kerb close.
Earlier an attempt to get copper over the technical target of $1,950 had failed leading to some selling.
Lead prices, which plunged on the kerb, edged back a couple of dollars more to $754/$757 having hit their lowest price in seven months earlier.
Aluminium, at a fresh nadir since June 1994 on the kerb, was indicated at $1,379/$1,380 up $1.50 and nickel was about $20 above kerb levels at $7,120/$7,140.
Tuesday's stocks data were expected to give copper prices at least some support with an expected a decline of 7,000-10,000 tonnes in inventories after Froday's fall of 9,300 tonnes.
